in_greek.name: Αλκυόνη
in_greek.long_meaning: Αλκυόνη είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'αλκυόνη', που σημαίνει 'κατερχόμενοι' ή 'πλέουσες'. Το όνομα αυτό συνδέεται με την ελληνική μυθολογία και την παράδοση της Εκκλησίας. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα Αλκυόνη δεν αναφέρεται άμεσα, αλλά η ετυμολογία του συνδέεται με την πλοήγη και την καθοδήγηση.

in_latin.name: Alcyone
in_latin.long_meaning: Alcyone is derived from the Greek word 'alkyōnē', meaning 'descending' or 'sailing'. This name has been used in Christian tradition to signify guidance and providence. The Latin Church adopted various Greek names, and Alcyone has been used in the context of Christian nomenclature to reflect heavenly guidance.

data.cultural_impact: Alcyone holds a rich cultural history as a name that originated from Greek mythology. In this myth, Alcyone was a woman known for her great love for her husband, Ceyx. Their love was so strong that when Ceyx died at sea, Alcyone threw herself into the sea in grief, and the gods took pity on her by transforming both of them into kingfishers, allowing them to spend eternity together in the sky. Thus, the name Alcyone often symbolizes enduring love and transformed devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: In a more spiritual sense, the Alcyone name carries the message of transformation, hope, and the eternal nature of love. As a Christian, Alcyone could be seen as a reminder of God's love that is constant and unchanging. The myth of Alcyone and Ceyx also serves as a powerful reminder of the transformative power of faith, as even in the face of great loss and despair, they were granted the gift of eternal life and love. Additionally, the Alcyone name could be interpreted as a call to keep faith in the face of adversity and to trust that God's love and grace will see us through even the darkest of times.
